name: Meshelemiah
title: Temple Gatekeeper
summary: Meshelemiah, also known as Shelemiah, was a Levite from the family of Korah who served as a gatekeeper at the Lord's temple in Jerusalem during King David's reign. He was placed in charge of the eastern gate and had several sons who also served as gatekeepers. His role was important for organizing the temple service that David prepared.

keyEvents.title: Appointed as Gatekeeper
keyEvents.description: Meshelamiah was appointed as one of the chief gatekeepers at the temple during David's organization of the Levites' service.

keyEvents.title: Sons in Service
keyEvents.description: Meshelamiah had seven sons who all served in the temple duties alongside their father, demonstrating the family's deep devotion to God.

keyEvents.title: Assigned Over the East Gate
keyEvents.description: Meshelamiah and his family were given responsibility for guarding the east gate at the temple, which was the main entrance.

keyEvents.title: Zachariah as Advisor and Gatekeeper
keyEvents.description: His son Zachariah was a wise advisor and was assigned to guard the north gate, showing the family's prominent position.

keyEvents.title: Part of Korah's Descendants
keyEvents.description: Meshelamiah belonged to the clan of Korah among the Levites, a lineage with a long tradition of temple service and worship.

keyEvents.title: Organization of Gatekeepers by Lot
keyEvents.description: Through casting lots, the duties of the gatekeepers were organized under David's leadership, and Meshelamiah's family received their assigned task.
